claims.content: The Customer wants to successfully register a new JTVauctions.com account as quickly as possible.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to successfully register a new JTVauctions.com account as quickly as possible.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: An unregistered Customer initiates registration and the system successfully establishes a new JTVauctions.com account for the Customer.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is unregistered and decides to register a new JTVauctions.com account.
scope_contract.success_boundary: A new JTVauctions.com account has been successfully established for the Customer.
variant_dimensions: Registration details/options are not specified in the goal evidence

claims.content: Customer
The Customer is unregistered and does not already have a JTVauctions.com account.
The Customer clicks the 'Register Now' link in the top navigation bar to create a free JTVauctions.com membership account.

The system presents Registration Page 1 (the 'short process'), which includes the User Information, My Payment Methods, and Terms of Use Agreement sections and collects the minimum required information to create an account.
The Customer enters First Name, Last Name, Email Address (entered twice), Password (8-12 characters, entered twice), and Member ID ('Handle').
The Customer selects a default payment method via the radio buttons in the My Payment Methods section (Credit Card, PayPal, or Amazon Payments).
The Customer checks the checkbox to accept and agree to the JTVauctions.com Terms of Use Agreement.
The Customer clicks the 'Finish Now' button to proceed to the second registration page to complete additional information.

The system displays Registration Page 2 with the headline 'Continuing Your Membership Creation' and sections for My Information, My Billing Address, My Shipping Address, My Shipping Preferences, and My Email Preferences, pre-populating the fields from Page 1 except the phone number.
The Customer enters or verifies the required My Information fields on Registration Page 2: Phone Number, Verify E-mail, New Password, and Verify Password.
The Customer provides billing address details (Address 1, Address 2, Suite/Apt, City, State, Zip Code, Country) and shipping details in the My Billing Address and My Shipping Address sections.
The Customer selects a shipping preference (USPS Standard or Expedited) in the My Shipping Preferences section.
The Customer sets email notification preferences (e.g., 'Please notify me via email when I am outbid') in the My Email Preferences section.
The Customer clicks the 'SAVE CHANGES' button to submit the registration information.

The system successfully establishes a new JTVauctions.com account for the Customer, displays a pop-up message instructing the user to add shop@jewelryTV.rsys1.com to their address book/white list/safe senders list and to enable cookies, and triggers an automated transactional email containing a Thank You message for registering and instructions to enable cookies and whitelist appropriate email addresses.

Diverges from Step 5: Instead of clicking the 'Finish Now' button to proceed to Registration Page 2, the Customer clicks the 'I Want to Sign In Now!' button. The system creates the new JTVauctions.com account and directs the Customer to the sign-in page, successfully establishing the account without collecting the additional Page 2 information.

Diverges from main_flow Step 2: Email Address fields (Create and verify) are required and must be entered twice; if the two email entries do not match, the email verification requirement is not satisfied. Exit: return to main_flow Step 2 to re-enter matching email addresses, then continue.

Diverges from main_flow Step 2: Password fields (Create and verify) must be 8 to 12 characters long and entered twice; if the password is not 8-12 characters or the two entries do not match, the Customer must re-enter a valid password. Exit: return to main_flow Step 2 to correct the password fields, then continue.

Diverges from main_flow Step 2: If the Customer enters a Member ID ('Handle') that is not unique in the database customer table, the system rejects it because the field label explicitly states '(Must be unique; can be email address)'. Exit: return to main_flow Step 2 to enter a different unique Member ID, then continue.

Diverges from main_flow Step 5: If the Customer clicks the grayed-out 'Finish Now' button before checking the Terms of Use checkbox, a popup message appears telling the Customer that they must read and agree to the Terms of Use before they can proceed. Exit: return to main_flow Step 4 to check the Terms of Use checkbox, then re-attempt Step 5.

Diverges from main_flow Step 11: If the Customer submits the registration using an email address that already exists in the customer table, the system notifies the Customer that the email address is already in use and asks whether they need to reset the password for that account. If the Customer indicates 'yes', the system generates an email to that address with a temporary password and advises the user to change it. If the Customer indicates 'no', no password-reset email is generated. Exit: in either case, the registration attempt terminates without creating a new account.

Diverges from main_flow Step 11: If, during account-creation validation after submission, the cross-reference against the Consumer Protection negative file matches the registrant, the registrant receives the message: 'We are sorry, we are unable to create an auction account for you at this time. If you believe this message to be in error, please contact our Customer Service team at: 800-550-8393.' Exit: the registration attempt terminates without establishing a new account.
The system successfully establishes a new JTVauctions.com account for the Customer.

The new account is persisted in the database with the unique Member ID ('Handle') defined by the Customer and the registration data collected (user information, default payment method, billing and shipping addresses, shipping preferences, and email notification preferences).
The system displays a pop-up message instructing the Customer to add shop@jewelryTV.rsys1.com to their address book/white list/safe senders list and to enable cookies in their web browser.
The system triggers an automated transactional email containing a 'Thank You' message for registering and instructions to enable cookies and whitelist appropriate email addresses.

quality_flags.detail: [exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 5 (duplicate email) only explicitly defines the exit for the 'yes, reset password' branch; the 'no, I do not need to reset password' branch is not given an explicit exit, so branch coverage is incomplete. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

inconsistency_hints: Main Flow's final step only states that the system successfully establishes the account. Postconditions additionally require a confirmation pop-up (whitelist/cookie instructions) and an automated transactional email, but no Main Flow step leads to these outputs. Therefore the last Main Flow step does not reasonably reach all Postconditions.

Exception flow claim 5 (index 4) handles a duplicate-email submission but only specifies the 'yes' path (send password-reset email). The 'Customer declines password reset' branch has no explicit exit, so that branch is not covered.

citation_audit.description: Structured author candidates captured before deterministic evidence-reference validation. Final slots remain evidence-valid.
